linkages: Firm-level financial data is linked with employee data in order to construct measures of investments in intangibles (LEED).
Employees are assigned to intangible types (OC, RD, ICT) through two- and three-digit ISCO-08 occupational codes.
Firms are assigned industry deflators at the two-digit NACE level.

sample.period: 2000-2013 (intangible stocks built from data starting in 1999)

construction_notes: Intangible investment = IA-type labour costs x working share x factor multiplier; the factor multiplier accounts for purchases of related intermediate goods and intangible capital and ranges from 1.48 for ICT to 1.76 for OC (Goerzig et al., 2010).
Working shares spent on producing intangibles: 20% for OC workers, 70% for RD workers, 50% for ICT workers.
Depreciation rates: OC 20% in manufacturing and 25% in services; RD 15%; ICT 33%. Growth rate g set at 2% for all IA.
Initial stock R(i,t=0) = N(i,t=0)/(delta + g), with N(i,t=0) the average growth-adjusted investment over a three-year period of the industry in the first year of data coverage.
Intangible investments are deflated with the producer price index for the business service industry; other nominal variables with industry-level producer price indexes.
Employees used in the production function exclude IA-type workers, to correct double counting of labour.
Intangible assets enter the TFP regression as beginning-of-year (lagged) values, in logs.
Capital is measured as total fixed assets reported in balance sheets for Denmark and as buildings plus machinery and equipment for Finland.
TFP is the residual of the first-stage Olley-Pakes production function, in logs.
